title: gold.sales_daily: the consumer guide
subtitle: What a team that reads gold.sales_daily needs to know, checked against the SQL, a 29-day sample, the query log, the checks and the run records, and what its documents get wrong.

verdict.text: Consumers cannot rely on it today. It has not been rebuilt since 2 November 07:35, store S-031 has been missing from it since 27 October, and the document gets the grain wrong. Its starter query adds EUR to HUF for the four Szeged stores. First fix the amount parse in `silver.orders` and add S-031 to `ref.stores`, then rerun the loads. Before any new team reads the table, correct the grain in the document and take `customer_email` out.

items.title: Stale since 2 November: silver.orders fails on a decimal comma
items.evidence: The last good build ended 2026-11-02T07:35, so the table holds orders up to 1 November. The builds of 3 and 4 November were skipped (`load_erp_orders failed for this delivery`), and `sales_daily_fresh` failed both days. `silver.orders` failed on 3 November (two attempts) and on 4 November with `invalid input syntax for type numeric: "18846,00"`, because the ERP now sends amounts with a decimal comma. All 1,038 and 1,013 lines of those deliveries have it. This is the same cause as the incident of 2026-09-14 (ops/incident-log.md:5). Its open item, `check the other ERP amount columns` (ops/incident-log.md:13), was never done. The run records end on 4 November, so the state on 10 November is not known.
items.fix: Cast with `util.parse_amount` (pipeline/functions/parse_amount.sql) in `silver.orders`, as `silver.invoices` has done since 15 September. Then reload the deliveries from 3 November on and run `build_sales_daily` by hand: it does not start by itself after a manual run (docs/howto/rerun-a-failed-job.md:8). Tell the five consumers which days were missing.

items.title: Store S-031 has been missing since 27 October: its order lines go to quarantine
items.evidence: From the delivery of 2026-10-28 on, about 100–125 lines a day with `store_id` S-031 were moved to quarantine by the `unknown_store_id` rule: 665 lines up to 2 November, and 115 and 109 more in the files of 3 and 4 November. Before that the rule caught 3–7 lines a day, all with S-000. `ref/stores.csv` has 30 stores and no S-031. Delivered lines grew from about 910 to about 1,020 a day at the same time. That is about 11% of the lines, none of them in `gold.sales_daily`. No check reports how many rows the quarantine takes. `orders_every_store_ordered` (checks/silver.yaml:13) only looks at stores already in `ref.stores`. [med] that S-031 is a new franchise store: README.md:3 still says 30 stores.
items.fix: Ask the ERP team or store operations what S-031 is. If it is a store, add it to `ref/stores.csv` and reload the deliveries from 28 October on. Add a check that fails when the quarantine takes more than a few lines a day.

items.title: The documented grain is wrong: it is one row per store, day and currency
items.evidence: The document says `one row per store and day`. On the sample, 42 of the 862 store-days have two rows: an EUR row and an HUF row, for the four Szeged stores S-027 to S-030. The SQL groups by `o.currency` (pipeline/gold/sales_daily.sql:21). The key check tests `sales_date, store_id, currency` (checks/gold.yaml:11), which is unique on all 904 rows. The document's starter query (docs/products/sales_daily.md:37-41) groups by `store_id` alone, so it adds HUF amounts to EUR amounts for those four stores.
items.fix: Change the grain in the document to `one row per store, day and currency`. Group the starter query by `store_id, currency` as well.

items.title: The currency column says EUR for Szeged; the table also has HUF
items.evidence: The document says `RSD for the Serbian stores, EUR for the Szeged stores`. In the sample, currency counts are RSD 754, EUR 108 and HUF 42. All 42 HUF rows belong to the four Szeged stores, on 22 days between 4 and 31 October. Each HUF row has one order and `kg_eq` 0. The source contract allows HUF (contracts/erp.yaml:52). `ref/stores.csv` gives EUR for all four HU stores. The BI board does not convert currencies (reports/bi/metrics.md:13). [guess] the HUF lines are a local charge with no goods behind them, such as a fee or a deposit.
items.fix: List the three currencies in the document. Ask the ERP team what the HUF lines are and write it down. Never sum amounts across currencies.

items.title: Net revenue has two definitions: the BI board deducts returns, the table does not
items.evidence: BI defines Net revenue as `gross revenue minus cancellations minus returns`. The product document (docs/products/sales_daily.md:28) says returns are not deducted. The SQL (pipeline/gold/sales_daily.sql:13) does not deduct them; it sums every line whose status is not `cancelled`. Board users therefore read a net revenue that still includes returns, and so does `Average order value` (reports/bi/metrics.md:10). The SQL also counts `on_hold` lines as net revenue, which neither definition mentions. Three such lines first appear in the file of 4 November.
items.fix: The BI team and finance settle one definition (`metric-spec`). Until then the BI document should say that returns are not deducted. The product document should say that on-hold lines are counted.

items.title: Every reader gets the franchisees' e-mail
items.evidence: `customer_email` comes from `silver.customers` through the left join at pipeline/gold/sales_daily.sql:20. It is filled in all 904 sample rows, with 30 distinct addresses. All five consumers read the table, 3,007 queries in 31 days, including the franchise portal and the store operations app. The stated purpose is `for finance's follow-ups` (docs/products/sales_daily.md:31). The document gives no legal reason and no access restriction.
items.fix: Drop `customer_email` from the served table. Finance can join `customer_id`, which stays in the table, to a restricted contacts table. Ask the franchise portal team whether one franchisee can see another franchisee's rows.

items.title: The document promises no time; the job and the runbook do, but differently
items.evidence: The document says `daily, after the ERP load`. The job has `sla: "08:00"` (jobs/build_sales_daily.yaml:8), and `sales_daily_fresh` tests it at 08:00 (checks/gold.yaml:3-7). The runbook gives `load_erp_orders` at 05:00 (docs/runbook.md:11), but the job runs at 06:30 (jobs/load_erp_orders.yaml:3) since 3e47102 (5 October). Weekday files arrived between 07:06 and 07:37 against the contract's `deliver_by: "06:00"` (contracts/erp.yaml:17). On those days the build ends around 07:35, about 25 minutes before the SLA. The 29 successful builds all met 08:00.
items.fix: Write the promise in the document: built by 08:00 Europe/Belgrade every day, with orders up to the day before. Correct the runbook.

items.title: One source check can never fail, and the table's totals are not checked
items.evidence: `orders_amount_positive` selects `where ... amount < amount`, which is never true, so it passed 29 times without testing anything. It has no bad-data case in checks/tests/cases.yaml. Only two checks cover the table itself, freshness and the key. No check compares its totals with `silver.orders` or the delivery, watches the quarantine volume, limits the currencies to a known set or covers stores that are missing from `ref.stores`.
items.fix: Change the query to `amount <= 0` and try it on a bad row. Add a check that the table's line count and gross amount per day match `silver.orders`, and a check on the quarantine volume.

items.title: No owner, no contract of its own, no change process
items.evidence: Questions go to `the data platform team`, with no person and no channel. The only contract that names the table is the ERP source contract, which lists it as a consumer (contracts/erp.yaml:61-63) and has `owner: TBD`. The SQL, the document and the job have not changed since 807306e (2026-07-20), and nothing says how five consumers would hear of a change.
items.fix: Name an owner and agree the contract draft under Releases and contract.

items.title: kg_eq looks unconverted, but the ERP's weight_g already converts pieces
items.evidence: The document says `pieces converted by product weight` (docs/products/sales_daily.md:29). The SQL takes `sum(o.weight_g) / 1000.0` as the ERP delivers it, and nothing in the pipeline converts pieces. All 42 HUF rows have `kg_eq` 0. BI's Tonnage, `kg_eq / 1000` (reports/bi/metrics.md:11), is consistent with the SQL.
items.reason: `weight_g` is the line's weight: on the order lines of 2 November, `weight_g` divided by `quantity` gives one fixed weight per product for all 24 products (90 pieces of P-1020 are 139,500 g, 1,550 g a piece). The pieces are converted in the ERP, the SQL sums the converted weights, and the document is right.

items.title: The job and the SQL name two consumers; the log shows five
items.evidence: The job description and the SQL comment (pipeline/gold/sales_daily.sql:1) name finance and the BI sales board. The query log also shows `store_ops_app`, `franchise_portal` and `regional_managers_report`, 744 reads each. The product document (docs/products/sales_daily.md:12-14) does list all five.
items.fix: Name all five in the job description so that whoever on call changes the job knows who is affected.

items.title: The source contract says amounts are integer cents; they arrive as decimals
items.evidence: The contract has `type: integer`, `unit: cents`. The deliveries carry decimals with a dot up to 2 November and with a comma since 3 November, and the sample has 105 rows with cents. `gross_revenue` and the other amounts are in currency units, not cents.
items.fix: Correct the source contract (`source-contract`), and write in the product document that amounts are in currency units with two decimals.

items.title: A day without orders has no row
items.evidence: Of the 870 store-days in the sample, 8 have no row: S-027 to S-030, twice each, on Fridays and Sundays. The document does not say that a missing row means no orders. Averages per day are wrong unless the days are counted from a calendar.
items.fix: Say it in the document; the starter queries below count days from a calendar.

blocks.text:
What each Acme Market franchise store ordered from Acme Foods per day: the number of orders and lines, gross, cancelled and net amounts, and the weight. The 26 Serbian stores order in RSD, the 4 Szeged stores in EUR and sometimes HUF.

**Built by** job `build_sales_daily` (jobs/build_sales_daily.yaml) at 07:00 Europe/Belgrade, after `load_erp_orders`. The job rebuilds the whole table from `pipeline/gold/sales_daily.sql`. Its sources are `silver.orders` (the ERP order lines, one ERP file a day holding the previous day's lines), `ref.stores` (kept by hand) and `silver.customers` (the ERP customer master).

**For whom:** finance's cash plan, which reads it once a morning, and four hourly readers: the BI sales board, the store operations app, the franchise portal and the regional managers' report.

**What it leaves out:** returns (in `silver.returns`), the lines of stores missing from `ref.stores` (quarantined, see Findings), and days on which a store did not order (no row, not a zero row).

items: Grain in the document
one row per store and day (docs/products/sales_daily.md:5): **wrong**
Real grain
one row per `sales_date`, `store_id` and `currency` [high]: unique on all 904 sample rows, the key the check tests (checks/gold.yaml:11), and the SQL's GROUP BY minus columns that depend on the store
Where it splits
42 store-days of S-027, S-028, S-029 and S-030 have an EUR row and an HUF row
What it does to a sum
summing over store and day adds HUF to EUR; always group by `currency` too
Days without orders
no row; 8 of 870 store-days in the sample, Szeged stores on Fridays and Sundays
History
none: the job rebuilds the whole table every day, so a past day changes if `silver.orders` changes
Size
about 25,200 rows (rows written by the build of 2 November); the sample is the last 29 days

sections.title: Starter queries
sections.intro: Each groups by currency, or filters on one. Check freshness first while the table is late.

blocks.title: 1. Is today's build there?
2. Net revenue per store for a month, in each currency
blocks.code:
select store_id, store_name, currency,
       sum(orders)       as orders,
       sum(net_revenue)  as net_revenue
from gold.sales_daily
where sales_date >= date '2026-10-01'
  and sales_date <  date '2026-11-01'
group by store_id, store_name, currency
order by currency, net_revenue desc;

blocks.title: 3. Daily totals per currency, never across currencies
blocks.code:
select sales_date, currency,
       sum(orders)            as orders,
       sum(gross_revenue)     as gross_revenue,
       sum(cancelled_amount)  as cancelled_amount,
       sum(net_revenue)       as net_revenue,
       sum(kg_eq) / 1000.0    as tonnes
from gold.sales_daily
where sales_date >= current_date - 7
group by sales_date, currency
order by sales_date, currency;

blocks.title: 4. Average order value per currency, as a ratio of sums
blocks.code:
select currency,
       sum(net_revenue) / nullif(sum(orders), 0) as avg_order_value
from gold.sales_daily
where sales_date >= date '2026-10-01'
  and sales_date <  date '2026-11-01'
group by currency;
-- returns are not deducted here; see Metric definitions

blocks.title: 5. Average per calendar day, counting days without orders as zero
blocks.code:
-- a store with no orders on a day has no row; count the days from a calendar
select store_id, currency,
       sum(net_revenue) / (date '2026-11-01' - date '2026-10-01') as net_revenue_per_day
from gold.sales_daily
where sales_date >= date '2026-10-01'
  and sales_date <  date '2026-11-01'
group by store_id, currency;

blocks.title: Contract draft: gold.sales_daily (for the owner to agree)
items: Owner
DRAFT: a named person in the data platform team, plus a channel for questions
Metric owners
DRAFT: finance and the BI team for net revenue; the ERP team for what the HUF lines mean
Grain and key
one row per `sales_date`, `store_id`, `currency`; no row when a store did not order
Columns

`sales_date` date; `store_id`, `store_name`, `currency` (RSD, EUR, HUF), `customer_id` text; `orders`, `order_lines` integer; `gross_revenue`, `cancelled_amount`, `net_revenue` numeric(12,2) in currency units; `kg_eq` numeric; `built_at` timestamp
Personal data
none: `customer_email` removed, contacts served from a restricted table
Freshness
built by 08:00 Europe/Belgrade every day, with orders up to the day before; a late build is announced to the consumers by 08:30
Completeness
every store that ordered in the ERP file appears; quarantined lines reported daily
Checks
key unique; fresh by 08:00; line count and gross amount per day equal `silver.orders`; currencies in the agreed set; quarantine below an agreed share
Changes
a breaking change (a column, the grain, a definition) announced to the five consumers two weeks ahead, with a release note in the document
Consumers
bi_sales_board, store_ops_app, franchise_portal, regional_managers_report, finance_cash_plan

The warehouse itself: only the 29-day sample (904 of about 25,200 rows), the ERP files of 2–4 November and the ops records, which end on 4 November. Whether the table has been rebuilt since then is not known.
What the HUF lines are, and whether S-031 is a real store.
What the franchise portal and the store operations app show, and to whom.
The BI board's own queries: only its metric document.
`silver.returns`, and how a reader could deduct returns.
The legal basis for serving the e-mail.

facts.scope: gold.sales_daily in acme-pipeline, the served daily sales table of Acme Foods

data.name: franchisee e-mail (customer_email)
data.rule: draft: not in the served table; finance reads it from a restricted table

assumptions: The ops records (runs, checks, quarantine, query log) cover 5 Oct – 4 Nov 2026 and are complete for that window.
open: Net revenue: BI deducts returns (reports/bi/metrics.md:8), the SQL does not (pipeline/gold/sales_daily.sql:13); BI and finance decide.
Grain: the document says store and day, the table is store, day and currency; the owner corrects the document and the starter query.
Currency: HUF lines for the Szeged stores are not documented; the ERP team says what they are.
Store S-031 is quarantined since 27 Oct; store operations confirm it and the data platform team adds it to ref.stores.
customer_email is served to all five consumers; the owner removes it or restricts it and states its purpose.
The table has no owner, no SLA in its document and no contract of its own.
